gpu.compute.bf16.note: 10 cores x 128 ALUs x 2 FLOP x ~1.58 GHz. No tensor cores on M4. Measured 2026-10-04 with benchmarks/compute.py: FMA-chain kernel, best of 20 (fp16 3.71). mx.matmul bf16 reaches 3.01-3.13 (n = 1024-8192). Short runs: burst, not sustained.

gpu.bandwidth.note: GPU-alone achievable bandwidth; upper-bounded by total_bandwidth. Measured 2026-10-03 with benchmarks/bandwidth.py, 1 GiB buffer, best of 20 (median 102.2). Write 94.9, copy 95.0 GB/s. Reads of 1-2 MiB reach ~250 GB/s; from 8 MiB up it is DRAM speed.

memory.total_bandwidth.note: LPDDR5X-7500, 128-bit; shared by CPU, GPU and ANE. Measured 2026-10-04 with benchmarks/contention.py (3 s read windows, best of 3): GPU alone 95.0, CPU alone 46-54, CPU + GPU 89.6-92.0 GB/s. Running both never beats the GPU alone, so these tests did not show a higher combined throughput; this does not certify a DRAM ceiling; `measured` is set to the GPU-alone read bandwidth from benchmarks/bandwidth.py.

gpu.usable_memory.note: MLX max_recommended_working_set_size (~17.76 GiB). iogpu.wired_limit_mb is 0 (system default), checked 2026-10-04.

capacity_assumptions.name: core
capacity_assumptions.note: Per-core on-chip SRAM: registers, threadgroup memory and cache. Since M3 (Dynamic Caching) these share one memory per core; Apple does not publish its size. benchmarks/hierarchy.py (2026-10-06): with one threadgroup per core, buffers up to 128-176 KiB are served at ~1.35 TB/s; with four groups per core the visible cache drops below 48 KiB, i.e. registers take the same SRAM. 512 KiB is a deliberate upper estimate (about 2x the largest observed cache), not a measurement.

capacity_assumptions.name: chip
capacity_assumptions.note: Bytes of on-chip storage the GPU sees between DRAM and its cores (GPU L2 plus system level cache), the M of the red-blue pebble bound. Unpublished; the estimate is the commonly reported 8 MB SLC. Measured 2026-10-04 with benchmarks/bandwidth.py --sweep-per-octave 4: reads stay at ~230 GB/s up to 2.4 MiB, fall gradually, and reach DRAM speed (~95 GB/s) at 11.3 MiB. `measured` takes the upper edge, rounded up to 12 MiB: a larger assumed M weakens the lower bound. The chosen upper edge is not a certified upper bound on physical capacity, so validity is conditional.

Since M3 (Dynamic Caching) these share one memory per core; Apple does not publish its size. benchmarks/hierarchy.py (2026-10-06): with one threadgroup per core, buffers up to 128-176 KiB are served at ~1.35 TB/s; with four groups per core the visible cache drops below 48 KiB, i.e. registers take the same SRAM. 512 KiB is a deliberate upper estimate (about 2x the largest observed cache), not a measurement.

capacity_assumptions.name: chip
capacity_assumptions.note: Bytes of on-chip storage the GPU sees between DRAM and its cores (GPU L2 plus system level cache), the M of the red-blue pebble bound. Unpublished; the estimate is the commonly reported 8 MB SLC. Measured 2026-10-04 with benchmarks/bandwidth.py --sweep-per-octave 4: reads stay at ~230 GB/s up to 2.4 MiB, fall gradually, and reach DRAM speed (~95 GB/s) at 11.3 MiB. `measured` takes the upper edge, rounded up to 12 MiB: a larger assumed M weakens the lower bound. The chosen upper edge is not a certified upper bound on physical capacity, so validity is conditional.

gpu.special.exp.note: exp/s (metal::fast::exp), the softmax resource: one exp per attention score. Measured 2026-10-06 with benchmarks/compute_shapes.py, 8 independent exp+fmul chains per thread; counted as a separate resource (max with FMA time, not added).
